source: NCERT Class VIII, Our Pasts III, History Ch. 8.

sections.heading: 1. The Emergence of Nationalism
points: Growing awareness that India was for Indians, and resentment of colonial exploitation, gave rise to **nationalism**.
The **Indian National Congress (INC)** was founded in **1885** (first session in **Bombay**, first president **W.C. Bonnerjee**; A.O. Hume played a role).
Early **Moderates** (Dadabhai Naoroji — 'Grand Old Man', **'drain of wealth' theory**; Gopal Krishna Gokhale; Pherozeshah Mehta) used **petitions, prayers and speeches**.

sections.heading: 2. Moderates to Radicals; Partition of Bengal
points: **Extremists / Radicals** (Bal Gangadhar **Tilak** — 'Swaraj is my birthright', Lala **Lajpat Rai**, Bipin Chandra **Pal** — the **'Lal-Bal-Pal'** trio) demanded **Swaraj (self-rule)** and used bolder methods.
**Partition of Bengal (1905)** by Lord Curzon sparked the **Swadeshi Movement** — boycott of British goods, promotion of **swadeshi (Indian)** goods.
The **Muslim League** was founded in **1906**.

sections.heading: 3. The Gandhian Era
points: **Mahatma Gandhi** returned from South Africa (1915); his method = **Satyagraha** (non-violent resistance).
Early struggles: **Champaran (1917, indigo), Ahmedabad mill strike, Kheda (1918)**.
**Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919, Amritsar)** and the **Rowlatt Act** fuelled anger.

sub: **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)** — boycott of schools, courts, titles, foreign cloth; withdrawn after **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.
**Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)** — began with the **Dandi Salt March** (breaking the salt law).
**Quit India Movement (1942)** — 'Do or Die'; demand for immediate British withdrawal.

sections.heading: 4. Towards Independence
points: **Purna Swaraj (complete independence)** declared at the **Lahore session (1929)**; **26 January 1930** observed as **Independence Day**.
**Subhas Chandra Bose** formed the **Indian National Army (INA/Azad Hind Fauj)**.
After WWII, negotiations (Cabinet Mission) and communal tensions led to **Partition**.
**India became independent on 15 August 1947**, but was **partitioned into India and Pakistan**, with terrible violence.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: INC founded 1885 (Bombay; W.C. Bonnerjee first president); Moderates → Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal).
Dadabhai Naoroji = 'drain of wealth'; Tilak = 'Swaraj is my birthright'.
Partition of Bengal 1905 → Swadeshi Movement; Muslim League 1906.
Gandhi: Champaran 1917; Non-Cooperation 1920–22 (ended after Chauri Chaura); Civil Disobedience/Dandi 1930; Quit India 1942.
Purna Swaraj declared at Lahore 1929; Independence 15 Aug 1947 (with Partition).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **INC founded in 1885**; **Muslim League in 1906**.
**Non-Cooperation (1920–22)** was called off after **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.
**Civil Disobedience (1930)** began with the **Dandi Salt March**; **Quit India = 1942 ('Do or Die')**.
**Purna Swaraj** was declared at the **Lahore session, 1929**.
